scope: Targeted literature search to inform a simulated learner audit of Parliamo; not a systematic review or an evaluation of the app's learning effectiveness.
selection: Prioritise original studies, research syntheses and publisher sources. Combine broad findings with language-specific evidence and recent replication; do not rank methods by publication date alone.

sources.title: Improving Students’ Learning With Effective Learning Techniques
sources.type: Research review; publisher summary and abstract consulted
sources.finding: Practice testing and distributed practice received high utility ratings. Self-explanation and interleaving received more conditional ratings.
sources.application: Keep low-stakes recall and later reviews central. Reading explanations remains useful preparation but should not be the sole practice.
sources.limit: Broad educational evidence does not validate this app, its timers or an Italian curriculum.

sources.title: The Effects of Spaced Practice on Second Language Learning: A Meta-Analysis
sources.finding: Across 48 experiments and 3,411 learners, spacing benefited second-language learning. Longer gaps helped delayed performance relative to shorter gaps; equal and expanding schedules were statistically equivalent.
sources.application: Preserve scheduled recall, shorter returns after difficulty and honest records of supported practice.
sources.limit: No basis for claiming the portal's exact 1/3/7/14-day schedule is optimal or that everyone needs an expanding schedule.

sources.title: Transfer of Test-Enhanced Learning: Meta-Analytic Review and Synthesis
sources.type: Meta-analysis; paper abstract and opening sections consulted
sources.finding: The review covered 122 experiments and found average transfer benefits from testing, with substantial dependence on the target task, elaborated retrieval and initial performance.
sources.application: Follow bounded recall with a short changed-detail response. Keep labels specific to observed recall rather than implying general speaking mastery.
sources.limit: This is not direct evidence that a portal retelling prompt improves spontaneous Italian conversation.

sources.title: Teaching L2 Learners How to Listen Does Make a Difference: An Empirical Study
sources.type: Semester study of 106 French learners in six intact classes; publisher abstract consulted
sources.finding: Learners guided through planning, monitoring, evaluation and problem solving outperformed a comparison group listening to the same texts equally often, controlling initial differences.
sources.application: Offer a compact listen-for-meaning routine: predict, catch the gist, replay one uncertain detail, compare, then explain what changed.
sources.limit: A brief optional interface prompt is a design inference, not a reproduction of the classroom intervention.

sources.title: Improving second language vocabulary learning and retention by leveraging memory enhancement techniques: A multidomain pedagogical approach
sources.finding: 48 Turkish university learners studied 64 English words over 17 days. Retrieval with feedback and spaced sessions produced larger gains than the comparison study/cramming regimen on the measured post-tests.
sources.application: Keep retrieval, useful feedback and subsequent return together rather than relying on repeated exposure alone.
sources.limit: The bundled intervention does not identify one independently optimal component; its results cannot be presented as expected gains for Parliamo users.

sources.title: Effects of spacing on the acquisition of explicit and implicit vocabulary knowledge: An approximate replication of Nakata and Elgort (2021)
sources.type: Replication with 69 Japanese learners and 48 pseudowords; publisher abstract consulted
sources.finding: Spacing improved measured explicit vocabulary knowledge. Neither schedule produced effective implicit-knowledge development in the semantic-priming measure, and schedules did not differ there.
sources.application: Separate word/grammar recall evidence from fluent spontaneous use; retain contextual listening and production alongside quizzes.
sources.limit: Pseudoword learning and semantic priming are narrow measures; the null result does not establish that spacing never helps implicit knowledge.

sources.title: The effects of interleaved and blocked corpus-based practice on L2 pragmatic development
sources.type: Language-learning experiment; publisher results and conclusions consulted
sources.finding: Interleaved practice benefited measured pragmatic accuracy, while blocked practice benefited fluency in the studied requests and suggestions.
sources.application: Keep a coherent topic within a short lesson; consider deliberate contrast practice for confusable forms after initial instruction.
sources.limit: Do not shuffle every exercise or claim that mixed practice is universally superior.

designPriorities: Preserve the difference between an independent first attempt and a corrected answer, including after reload.
Make recommendations appropriate to the learner's actual saved course and programme; missing evidence is not a weakness.
Make listening purposeful before revealing text, and offer a small transfer task after comprehension.
Retain bounded review sessions, bilingual support and reversible navigation instead of adding pressure or an unbounded backlog.
evaluationNext: After these usability repairs, an actual learner could compare recall on new prompts several days later and attempt an unfamiliar short conversation with a teacher. Agent simulations and passing browser tests cannot establish learning gains.
